text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream in us-west-2 (hosted). p95 jumped 120ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~6.2s, streaming stalls observed. Paging oncall.
Alex (oncall): Seen. Starting triage. Is this global or region-only? Any customer 5xxs? @Leah can you check support tickets?
Leah (support): No 5xxs in the ticket queue yet, but two customers reported degraded streaming responsiveness in us-west-2. No errors, just hangs in client logs.
Jen (sre): Graphs show tail at the continuous-batching runtime. Pod-level CPU steady, GPU SM util spiky. KV cache eviction rate up ~3x. I suspect padding amplification from mixed-seqlen packing.
Sam (eng-runtime): That matches an ongoing regression in the packer heuristics we shipped last week. Under heterogenous seq-lengths it overpacks and preemption fairness lets small requests wait behind large ones -> tail.
Ryan (ml): Any model fallbacks available? We could route heavy customers to smaller/quantized variant temporarily.
Alex (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) Disable streaming batch packing on affected pool 2) Reduce max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 512 3) Apply temporary per-tenant isolation for the two noisy customers 4) Route new stream sessions to fallback model variant in us-west-2.
Sam (eng-runtime): I'll flip packer to conservative mode on the pool. Command:

```
# disable stream packer on pool-usw2
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control-plane/api/pools/usw2/packers/stream/disable
```
Sam (eng-runtime): Also lowering scheduler packing threshold:
```
PATCH /api/scheduler/config
{"max_batch_tokens":512, "fairness_beta":0.8}
```
Jen (sre): Doing the node-side change now. kubectl patch on runtime deployment to set env SCHED_MAX_BATCH=512 so it survives restarts.
Alex (oncall): Leah, can you create a customer-facing note? Short: we saw elevated tail latency for streaming in us-west-2, mitigation in progress, possible short interruptions.
Leah (support): Drafted and queued, link: https://intra/docs/incidents/1768123456/customer-note (will send after Alex ok)
Alex (oncall): Go ahead.
IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Action taken: packer disabled on pool-usw2 by Sam at T+3m. Scheduler config patched at T+5m.
Jen (sre): After mitigations p95 back to ~150ms, p99 reduced to ~900ms within 7 minutes. Streaming stall counts dropped 78%.
Ryan (ml): Looks better. Root cause hypothesis: packer heuristic prioritized maximizing GPU throughput, but with high variance seq lengths it created giant batches that blocked small realtime streams. Combined with a fairness weight bug, preemption didn't evict large batches quickly.
Sam (eng-runtime): Confirmed. The packer change this week introduced a greedy fill mode for streaming to increase token throughput. It didn't respect tenant-level max-pending and had an off-by-one in fairness scoring.
Alex (oncall): Short-term followups (assign): Sam - revert greedy fill or add tenant max-pending guard (ETA 4h). Jen - monitor us-west-2 at 5m cadence and keep pager open. Ryan - prepare fallback rollout plan for two affected customers (ETA 2h). Leah - notify customers that mitigation applied and we'll follow up with postmortem.
Jen (sre): I'll add an alert to detect padding amplification: if avg_batch_token_stddev > 1.5x baseline and p99 > 2s then page.
Sam (eng-runtime): I'll push a hotfix branch to revert greedy fill and include unit tests for fairness scoring.
Ryan (ml): We should also consider model-level soft-quotas for long-seq customers or explicit route to batch-only endpoints.
Leah (support): Customers copied. Two want status updates every 30m; I'll coordinate.
Alex (oncall): Handoff: I'm taking next 30m to stabilize, then Jen will own active watch for the next 6 hours. Sam you keep PR for hotfix. If anything flares, escalate to paging priority 1.
Sam (eng-runtime): Hotfix PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2381 - includes revert and guard. CI running.
Jen (sre): Temporary dashboards: https://grafana/internal/d/streampack-usw2 showing p50/p95/p99, batch size distribution, per-tenant queue depths.
IncidentBot: Note: This incident has been logged as INC-2026-0457 and will auto-create postmortem template.
Alex (oncall): Thanks team. Quick retro items: avoid greedy packer default in prod; add tenant-rate/seqlen isolation; add chaos test for mixed-seqlen workloads in canary.
Leah (support): I'll gather impacted customer IDs and prod logs, attach to postmortem.
Ryan (ml): After hotfix, we should run a synthetic workload: 70% short seqs (<=32), 30% long seqs (>=1024) at 2x normal qps to validate fairness.
Sam (eng-runtime): Scheduling note I'll implement: when batch_token_size variance high, fall back to size-capped packing and lower pack window to 10ms.
Jen (sre): Monitoring shows stable for 45m. Closing the active pager, keep watch channel open for 6h. I'll escalate if metrics deviate.
Alex (oncall): Officially handing off to Jen for watch. Final status: mitigation successful, customers notified, hotfix PR in flight, postmortem owner assigned (Sam).
